title: SnipStream: atomic adminlets for incremental remediation and runbooks-as-tasks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a lightweight library of composable, idempotent admin primitives ("adminlets") and a runtime (SnipStream) that executes runbooks-as-tasks. Goal is to enable on-call and ops engineers to craft small, auditable, and reversible remediation flows that can be executed programmatically or from the Console. This complements existing runbook services by offering tiny, testable constructs optimized for fast, incremental remediation of common operator tasks.
acceptance_criteria: Adminlet SDK published to internal PyPI and npm with README and basic examples
SnipStream runtime can execute an adminlet bundle with dry-run and checkpoint modes
All adminlet executions produce structured audit events (logs + audit entries) and are surfaced in Console runbook history
RBAC gated: only users with ops:remediate can execute production-impact adminlets; feature flag gated rollout
Automated unit and integration tests cover idempotency, rollback, and error-handling behaviors
technical_notes: Adminlets are implemented as small script modules with a deterministic input schema (JSON Schema) and explicit output contract (status, delta, artifacts)
SnipStream will provide a safe execution sandbox with timeouts, resource limits, and a dry-run mode that only emits proposed deltas without committing changes
Integrations planned: Vault/KMS for credential fetch, audit-log forwarder to syslog+Console, and Ops routing for canary vs global execution
Fallback behavior: if an adminlet fails, SnipStream supports automatic rollback hooks and a fail-open to a read-only incident note rather than partial mutation
We will reuse the runbook provenance schema from ENG-421007 to maintain consistent traceability across tools
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal ops team + 2 SREs enabled via internal flag (week 1)
Beta: expand to oncall rotating engineers and solutions team; collect metrics and feedback (week 2-3)
Canary release on a subset of production namespaces with read-only default; require explicit approval to enable write-mode (week 4)
GA: enable for all orgs once metrics meet safety thresholds and postmortem checklist completed (week 6)
telemetry: Event: snipstream.exec.start with fields: adminlet_id, caller_id, mode (dry|live), namespace
Event: snipstream.exec.end with fields: status, duration_ms, error_code
Alert: >3 failed live execs in 10m for the same adminlet -> PagerDuty oncall
Dashboard: per-adminlet success rate, median duration, cost estimate per-run
Tracing: propagate trace IDs to downstream infra calls for latency breakdowns
comments: 2026-03-01 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket after incident-2026-02-25 where partial manual remediation caused drift. Proposed atomic adminlets to reduce human error and improve auditability.
2026-03-03 - Liam Chen: Drafted SDK API and basic adminlet schema. Decided to use JSON Schema for inputs to simplify validation across languages.
2026-03-05 - Design review (Kara Nguyen): UI should surface 'dry-run' diffs inline and prevent blind acknowledgement. Agreed to show delta preview and require explicit confirmation for write-mode.
2026-03-07 - Security (Marta Ivanov): Requested KMS integration and allowlist enforcement for credential-fetching adminlets. Marked security_review_required=true and added dependency on ENG-762001.
2026-03-09 - Eng review (Paul Rodriguez): Implementation trade-off: embed sandbox vs run in short-lived sidecar. Chose sidecar approach to leverage existing language runtimes and reduce blast radius.
2026-03-11 - CI: initial test harness added on PR #482. Observed flakiness in integration test where Vault responses were mocked; added deterministic VCR recordings.
2026-03-12 - Liam Chen: Feature flag gate created (snipstream.alpha). Next: add audit-forwarder and Console runbook history integration. Blocker: need Ops Console consent for UI change (pinging PM).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: adminlet executes destructive action unexpectedly -> Mitigation: default to dry-run, explicit write confirmation, RBAC + approval process
Risk: credential leakage from scripts -> Mitigation: credential fetch via Vault KMS only; no inline secrets in adminlet bundles
Risk: operational complexity with many small adminlets -> Mitigation: cataloging + tagging in Console, recommended templates and ownership fields
Risk: audit blindspots -> Mitigation: structured audit events forwarded to centralized logging and immutable audit log retention
qa_plan: Unit tests for each adminlet verifying idempotency across repeated runs
Integration tests with a sandboxed infra environment (namespaced test cluster)
Chaos test: simulate partial network failures to verify rollback hooks
Manual verification: run a curated set of adminlets in dry-run then approve live execution under supervision
next_steps: Add audit-forwarder and map events to Console runbook history API
Coordinate Console UI change with PM (Kara) and schedule alpha rollout
Prepare runbook templates for the top 10 oncall remediation tasks and author 5 adminlets as examples
